The usual parenteral dose for all indications apart from nausea and vomiting is 25 to 50 mg; a dose of 100 mg should not be exceeded. Doses of 12.5 to 25 mg, re- peated at intervals of not less than 4 hours, may be giv- en for the treatment of nausea and vomiting, although not more than 100 mg is usually given in 24 hours. Children aged 5 to 10 years may be given 6.25 to 12.5 mg of promethazine hydrochloride by deep intra- muscular injection. Promethazine has been used topically to provide relief in hypersensitivity disorders of the skin and for burns but, as with other antihistamines, it may produce skin sensitisation. Sedation. For reference to the use of lytic cocktails of chlorpro- mazine, promethazine, and pethidine, and the view that alterna- tives should be considered in children, see under Pethidine, p.115.
